clue.text: Leading scholar close to screen for film about space

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

blocks.note: leading means in front of everyone else
a Master of Arts is a scholar in crossword shorthand
the final letter of screen

explanation.surface: A top academic is near the cinema screen for a space movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2018 film about Neil Armstrong and the first Moon landing is called First Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2018 biopic follows Neil Armstrong's journey to the Moon, so it is literally a movie about spaceflight.

clue.text: Leave helpless certain element

blocks.note: first meaning: to leave someone stuck with no way out, as on a shore
second meaning: one thread or part of a story or argument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' tempts a chemistry answer, but here it means one component, such as a thread in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to maroon someone without resources; as a noun it is a single thread or component of something larger.

clue.text: Wooden soprano given a listing?

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for soprano
a ship with a list leans to one side

explanation.surface: A soprano is handed a place on a list, or perhaps a stiff performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listing' suggests being put on a list, but it means leaning over, as a ship lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or acting is stiff and unnatural, the same figurative sense as calling a performance wooden.

clue.text: Tragic figure caught on sign over sunless Greek city

indicators.note: without sun means the letter S, short for sun, is taken away

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
Patras is a port city in western Greece

explanation.surface: Someone is caught by a road sign above a Greek city with no sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' and 'over' place each piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen died by suicide and is the heroine of Shakespeare's tragedy Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Music maker in top boozer on a regular basis

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A musician plays regularly in the best pub in town.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a double-reed woodwind instrument, and any instrument produces music when played.

clue.text: Quiet woman at work is Irish banker

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
a woman's name
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A shy woman employed in finance works for a bank in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the longest river in Ireland, and rivers are crossword bankers because they flow between banks.

clue.text: Name a pad that’s prepared Spanish turnover

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked up from raw ingredients, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to name a flat that has been made ready, like a Spanish property sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' sounds like business revenue, but it is a folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a pastry folded over a filling, and this stuffed pastry is a staple of Spanish cooking.

clue.text: Hard metal manufactured in small rural settlement

indicators.note: something manufactured has been made into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tough metal is being produced in a little country village.
explanation.definitionFit: The word denotes a village too small to have its own church, a tiny countryside community.

clue.text: Completely enthusiastic about short story

indicators.note: a short version of a word has its final letter cut off

blocks.note: being into something means being keen on it
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly keen on a brief piece of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all things considered or added up, an adverbial synonym for entirely.

clue.text: Recall outstanding writer with endless tramp in area for artists?

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the whole string is read from end to start
with no end means the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I for the figure one
the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me
a hobo is a wandering homeless person

explanation.surface: Remembering a brilliant author who lived like a vagrant in an artists' quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Bohemia is really a region of the Czech Republic; the artistic sense comes from bohemian lifestyles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemian artists gave their name to any unconventional community of creative people, so the region stands for such a quarter.

clue.text: Thing worn over the shoulders in rickshaw, lately

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words, spanning them

blocks.note: the end of rickshaw runs on into the start of lately

explanation.surface: Someone recently riding in a rickshaw had something draped round them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a piece of fabric draped around the upper body and arms for warmth or decoration.

clue.text: Loan Dane arranged to include pounds for the public?

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a fresh order, so the letters move
to include something is to take it inside, so a letter goes within the jumble

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Danish man is lent money for the benefit of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everybody without exception, which is what the whole public amounts to.

clue.text: Primitive set of dishes covering messy dive

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one part goes around the other
something messy is in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a meal is a set of courses
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A basic set of crockery is spread across a scruffy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A dive is a seedy bar, which helps the surface but is just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word describes anything crude or backward, as if belonging to the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Where one drinks in sweltering Australian city

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: sweltering weather is very hot
a bar is where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Drinking somewhere in a sweltering Australian town.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Tasmania, the island state in the south of Australia.

clue.text: What concerns ethicist about origin of this human trait

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part goes round the other
the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: ethics is the study of right and wrong
the first letter of this

explanation.surface: A moral philosopher worries about where a human characteristic comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Being destined to die is a defining condition of being human, setting people apart from gods.

clue.text: Standard name in Paris to describe Republican

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one part encircles another

blocks.note: nom is French for name
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A standard name used in Paris to label a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' is used in its geometric sense of tracing a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or expected level, a benchmark against which other things are measured.

clue.text: Option concerning Cheltenham, perhaps

blocks.note: re means with regard to
Cheltenham, in Gloucestershire, is a famous English racecourse; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Choosing something to do with the Cheltenham races.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse to something means turning to it as a possible remedy or alternative.

clue.text: Good space for stable employee

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
room means space

explanation.surface: Plenty of room is needed for someone who works in the stables.
explanation.definitionFit: This worker looks after horses, brushing and feeding them in their stalls.

clue.text: Stick note in bundle

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: a wad is a bundle, as of banknotes
N is short for note

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a banknote into a roll of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb, but the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's slender rod is a thin length of wood, which is what a stick is.

clue.text: Absurdly small and unusually sorry side with no end of duds

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are rearranged
with no means lacking, so a letter is removed from the fodder
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of duds

explanation.surface: A pathetically small and regretful team without a single failure at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: One S is removed from sorry side before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisory offer is so low it invites ridicule, laughably inadequate in amount.

clue.text: Tips for tutee a prominent feature in informal educational meeting

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of tutee
taken as written
a jutting chin is a prominent facial feature

explanation.surface: Advice for a student about a notable thing at an informal class.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a 1960s style of open discussion forum on a topical issue, held at a college.

clue.text: Gangster in largely hideous US city ring uncovered

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the last letter is dropped
with the cover stripped off, the outside letters at both ends go

blocks.note: vile means hideous
LA is Los Angeles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mobster in an ugly American city has his ring gang exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a criminal, and a criminal is the classic bad guy or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Irish playwright cited martyr

indicators.note: cited sounds like sighted but means quoted, spoken out, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: Samuel Beckett wrote Waiting for Godot

explanation.surface: An Irish dramatist is quoted as a martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishop Thomas of Canterbury was murdered in his cathedral in 1170 and canonised as a saint.

clue.text: British selector losing power in quarrel

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: B is short for British
a picker selects things
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A British team selector loses influence during an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to argue petulantly about trivial matters, which is what a squabble is.

clue.text: Part-time journalist resting after recreation around end of summer

indicators.note: re-creation means making anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a different order
around means surrounding, so the jumble goes outside a letter
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: A freelance reporter takes a break after some leisure time at the end of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recreation' reads as leisure, but split it as re-creation and it becomes the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper pays such a correspondent per story rather than employing them on the staff.

clue.text: European entering ravine is pilot on a set course

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one letter goes into the other word

blocks.note: a gorge is a ravine
E is short for European

explanation.surface: A European flies a plane straight down a steep valley.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old pilots' slang for an aircraft's autopilot, which keeps it on a set course.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic steering device after a person, the robot that flies a plane on a fixed heading.

clue.text: Dramatist is mean-spirited type about much of Spanish-speaking country

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part wraps around the other
much of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a churl is a rude, surly person
Chile speaks Spanish

explanation.surface: A playwright is described as a nasty piece of work concerning a South American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Caryl Churchill is a British playwright, author of Top Girls; the obvious Winston is not the dramatist meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Caryl Churchill is a leading modern British playwright, author of Top Girls and Cloud Nine.

clue.text: Pair in lift beam at intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals means skipping letters, taking every second one

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Two people working on the girders of a lift shaft, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a couple seen as being romantically involved are described as one unit.

clue.text: Views the smallest room with walls in Kansas

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outside letters at each end

blocks.note: the smallest room is a jokey British euphemism for the toilet, and loo is British for toilet
the first and last letters of Kansas

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the tiny toilet in a Kansas house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs for directing your gaze at something, so one substitutes for the other.

clue.text: Like some bathrooms in clubs, say, in three directions

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: E, N and E are compass points
clubs are an example of a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Some bathrooms come in three directions at the club.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom described this way is attached directly to a bedroom, from French for following on.

clue.text: Activate tense person to work on sails

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a rigger fits a ship's ropes and sails

explanation.surface: An anxious sailor is set to work on the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or start it working, a verb synonym.
